events.n: Captivating Clay: Contemporary Japanese Ceramics from the Horvitz Collection
events.d: April 13, 2024 — January 03, 2027 Today, Japanese ceramic artists are building on centuries of tradition and taking the art in dynamic and new directions. events.n: Wall Power! Spectacular Quilts from the American Folk Art Museum
events.d: October 17, 2026 — January 10, 2027 Quilts are America’s great art experiment: monumental compositions in color, pattern, geometry and representation, and traditionally, quilts are made mostly by women. events.n: Power of Remembrance: AIDS Memorial Quilt Panels
events.d: October 17, 2026 — January 03, 2027 The AIDS Memorial Quilt is a labor of love begun by volunteers. Quilting has long been a communal activity, bringing people together to create something useful, passing down stories and traditions from one generation to another. The AIDS Memorial Quilt was first imaged by Human rights activist Cleve Jones in 1985 from his desire to remember those who had died from AIDS-related illnesses.
